examples.question_text:
Rewrite each division as an equivalent division with a whole-number divisor.
a. $0.742\div0.06$
b. $19\div0.007$
examples.solution_text:
a. $0.06$ has $2$ decimal places. Multiply both numbers by $100$.
$0.742\times100=74.2$ and $0.06\times100=6$.
$0.742\div0.06=74.2\div6$
b. $0.007$ has $3$ decimal places. Multiply both numbers by $1000$.
$19\times1000=19000$ and $0.007\times1000=7$.
$19\div0.007=19000\div7$
Multiplying both numbers by the same power of $10$ leaves each quotient unchanged.

examples.question_text:
Divide using the division algorithm.
a. $7.236\div0.03$
b. $29\div0.4$
examples.solution_text:
a. Multiply both numbers by $100$.
$7.236\div0.03=723.6\div3$.
Divide from left to right: $7\div3=2$ remainder $1$, $12\div3=4$, $3\div3=1$, then $6\div3=2$. Keep the decimal point above the dividend’s decimal point.
$\begin{array}{r}241.2\\[-2pt]3\,\big)\overline{723.6}\end{array}$
$7.236\div0.03=241.2$.

b. Multiply both numbers by $10$.
$29\div0.4=290\div4$.
Write $290$ as $290.0$ to continue the division. Divide from left to right: $29\div4=7$ remainder $1$, $10\div4=2$ remainder $2$, then $20\div4=5$. Keep the decimal points lined up.
$\begin{array}{r}72.5\\[-2pt]4\,\big)\overline{290.0}\end{array}$
$29\div0.4=72.5$.

Multiply both numbers by $1000$ to make the divisor whole.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}1.4\div0.002\\&=1400\div2\end{aligned}$
Since $14\div2=7$, $1400\div2=700$.
$1.4\div0.002=700$.

examples.derivation: a. Scaling both numbers by 100 gives 723.6 ÷ 3. Successive division gives 2 remainder 1, then 4, 1 and 2 tenths, so the quotient is 241.2. Check: 241.2 × 0.03 = 7.236. b. Scaling both numbers by 10 gives 290 ÷ 4. Dividing 290.0 gives 7 remainder 1, then 2 remainder 2, then 5 tenths, so the quotient is 72.5. Check: 72.5 × 0.4 = 29. Both algorithm representations agree with the prose and answers.
Multiplying both numbers by 1000 gives 1400 ÷ 2. Since 14 ÷ 2 = 7, place value gives 1400 ÷ 2 = 700. Check: 700 × 0.002 = 1.4. The opening expression has the required phantom equals gutter.
